evals.prompt: /critical-review I want to build a multi-tenant SaaS app where each customer gets their own isolated Postgres database (database-per-tenant model). My reasoning: better data isolation, easier to comply with data residency laws, and simpler backup/restore per customer. The backend is Node.js/Express. I plan to spin up a new RDS instance per tenant on signup. Auth is handled by a JWT issued by a central auth service, with the tenant ID embedded in the token. The app itself is stateless and connects to whichever DB the token says. Should be easy to scale.
evals.expected_output: Three distinct perspective reports (Antagonist, Researcher, Advocate) followed by an aggregated synthesis covering strengths, weaknesses, what to keep, what to change, and concrete recommendations.
expectations: Output contains three separate reports with headers for Antagonist, Researcher, and Advocate
Output contains an aggregated/synthesis section at the end
The aggregated section includes strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations
The Antagonist report raises specific technical concerns (e.g., cost, cold start, connection limits, RDS overhead)
The Researcher report names at least one real existing solution or approach (e.g., row-level security, schema-per-tenant, Neon, PlanetScale, Citus)
The Advocate report identifies genuine strengths of the approach (e.g., isolation, compliance)
The recommendations section contains concrete actionable items

evals.prompt: /critical-review here's my plan for a football content generation agent: there's a Curator agent that pulls data from sports APIs and news feeds, a Writer agent that takes the curated data and generates articles/tweets/analysis, and a Critic agent that reviews the Writer's output for accuracy and quality before publishing. The three agents talk to each other sequentially — Curator feeds Writer, Writer feeds Critic, Critic either approves or sends back to Writer. Everything is orchestrated by a parent agent. I'm building this on top of Google ADK. The goal is fully automated sports content that feels human-written. Monetization is via a newsletter subscription.
evals.expected_output: Three distinct perspective reports (Antagonist, Researcher, Advocate) followed by an aggregated synthesis covering strengths, weaknesses, what to keep, what to change, and concrete recommendations.

The aggregated section includes strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations

The Advocate report highlights genuine strengths like the pipeline separation of concerns or the quality-gate via Critic
The recommendations section contains at least 3 concrete actionable items

evals.prompt: /critical-review I'm designing a local-first collaborative note-taking app. The core idea: all data lives on the user's device (SQLite), and sync between devices is handled via CRDTs (conflict-free replicated data types). There's no central server — peers sync directly over WebRTC when on the same network, and fall back to an optional self-hosted relay server for cross-network sync. The app is an Electron desktop app + React Native mobile. Monetization: one-time purchase, no subscription. My pitch is privacy, offline-first, and no vendor lock-in.
